text:
maya_support: Heads up - KestrelAI reported unexpected burst charges on their May invoice. They have a 3-node reserved commit but ~12 node-hours billed as burst on 05/12. Can finance/ops take a quick look?

kevin_fin: Thanks Maya. Paste invoice snippet and the reserved pool tag?

maya_support: INV-2026-0512 in the ticket. Pool tag: kest-rel-3. Billing bot snippet:
```
Invoice: INV-2026-0512
Period: 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-31
Line items:
 - Reserved capacity (kest-rel-3): 3 nodes - $6,000
 - Burst usage (burst-unallocated): 12 node-hours - $180
Total: $6,180
```

sam_ops: Pulled meter logs. Short story: agent version 1.4.2 used an internal tag "kest-rel3" (no hyphen) for a ramp event. Aggregator didn't map aliases -> hours flowed to burst. Looks like a packaging mismatch in older AMI.

kevin_fin: Can ops export node-level rows for 05/12? Need node_id, ts, seen_tag to justify invoice adjustment. Estimate of delta?

sam_ops: Export attached: 12 node-hours misattributed, estimated delta $180. All rows safe to retag. Backfill job bf-2026-519 scheduled.

lina_revops: Record: revops-834 created, attaching export and backfill id.

rachel_sales: Sales agrees to invoice correction only. No SLA credit required; customer small but vocal.

kevin_fin: I'll create credit memo CM-2026-155 for $180 (reason: METER_ALIAS_MISATTRIB). Routing to AP for posting. Please wait to send customer note until credits post.

ops-bot: Backfill bf-2026-519 completed successfully, 12 rows re-associated to kest-rel-3. No conflicts.

maya_support: Sent short note: "We corrected a metering tag mismatch and applied a $180 invoice adjustment. Apologies for the confusion." Customer replied: "Thanks, all good."

kevin_fin: AP posted credit; closing out. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
